conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and any children you're responsible for.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children that you're responsible for? If so, could you please tell me their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have three children. There's Alex who is 7, Blake who is 20, and Charlie who is also 7.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have three children: Alex (7), Blake (20), and Charlie (7).

Let me ask you a few clarifying questions to assess your eligibility for each of them.

**First, do you live with all three of these children in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and all three of them live with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. That's helpful information.

Now, since Blake is 20 years old, I need to check their circumstances more carefully. 

**Is Blake currently in approved education or training (such as college, university, or an apprenticeship)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Blake isn't in any education or training at the moment. They're actually working full-time now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. 

**How many hours per week does Blake work in their full-time job?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: They work full-time, so that's around 35-40 hours a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Now let me ask about Alex and Charlie. Since they're both 7 years old and living with you in the UK:

**Are Alex and Charlie in any hospital, care, or residential accommodation at the moment, or do they live with you full-time at home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex is actually fostered by me, but the council doesn't pay me anything for their accommodation or maintenance. Charlie lives with me full-time at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's very helpful information, thank you. Just to confirm a few final details:

**Are you currently receiving any of the following benefits: Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not currently receiving any of those benefits myself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that information. I now have all the details I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for each of your three children.

Let me explain the outcome:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Summary

Based on your circumstances, here's your eligibility status:

✅ **Alex (7 years old)** - **ELIGIBLE**
You can claim Child Benefit for Alex. As you're fostering Alex and the local council is not paying anything towards their accommodation or maintenance, you meet the fostering criteria for Child Benefit.

❌ **Blake (20 years old)** - **NOT ELIGIBLE**
You cannot claim Child Benefit for Blake. Even though they're under the normal upper age limit for certain circumstances, Blake is working full-time (35-40 hours per week) and is not in approved education or training. This means they no longer qualify under Child Benefit rules.

✅ **Charlie (7 years old)** - **ELIGIBLE**
You can claim Child Benefit for Charlie. As Charlie is under 16, lives with you in the UK, and you're responsible for their upkeep, you meet the standard criteria for Child Benefit.

If you haven't already done so, you can make a claim for Alex and Charlie. If you have any further questions or need additional support, you can contact the Child Benefit Office.

This condition is met, so you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Therefore, you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Blake.

There are no special circumstances affecting eligibility (such as hospital or care placements). Therefore, you qualify for Child Benefit for Charlie.
